correctness.rationale: For each fixed signed block partition the unique weighted-TV minimizer is affine in lambda. The absolute gap derivative across adjacent blocks is bounded by the signed-mass chord deficit of the edge penalty profile and is nonpositive precisely under mass-concavity; piecewise-affine continuity gives the global all-data statement. A strictly increasing datum proves necessity for local gap shrinkage, while an exact local KKT construction with positive lambda_- < lambda_+ proves genuine positive-interval fusion then unfusion for every failed inequality. The three-site rational witness has been checked exactly and a standalone enumerator passed finite KKT tests; numerical tests do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: Bento, Furmaniak and Ray (2018, Sections II-IV) analyze arbitrary weighted 1D fused-lasso paths, prove quadratic event bounds and give unfusion examples, but do not assert the sharp mass-coordinate concavity equivalence or monotonicity of every individual jump magnitude. Their stated open direction concerns weights under which path events simplify. The 2004 introduction and 2013 unweighted TV solver do not imply the present classification. A superficially similar mass-concavity criterion for weighted isotonic projection is a different two-input stability question. These comparisons support originality within searched literature, but do not certify priority.

value.rationale: Monotone fusion is a key simplification in 1D TV regularization, but arbitrary weight profiles can cause splitting. The theorem supplies the exact local and mass-aware all-data design criterion valid in every finite dimension, strengthens it to monotonicity of every edge gap, and constructs a real finite fusion/unfusion interval whenever the criterion fails. This is a motivated complete classification for a natural proximal family, not a single case or routine computation.
